the electronic transport properties of InAs nanowires.
the electronic transport of a quantum wire in a strong transverse magnetic field and the influence of a charged tip on its transport properties.

the top subband and the disordered sea are the two distinct electron populations in the InAs wire, and they are affected differently by the tip of the atomic force microscope.
we are able to control the number of electrons on the top subband of the wire, and we are able to detect the number of electrons occupying the disordered sea of the wire.

the tip-to-sample separation plays a significant role in the ability to locally control the top subband and the disordered sea, which in turn is a function of the electron concentration in the wire.
the quasi-periodic oscillation of the conductance is a direct result of a periodic modulation of the conductive subband electrons in a disordered sea.

the tip of an atomic microscope can be used to locally affect and detect the electronic properties of a quantum wire.
